posts.raw_content:
Have y'all ever heard of Ordo Amoris? Its a Christian theology created by St. Augustine explaining the essence of how Christian morality works. It states that most sin does not come from loving bad things so much as loving good things in the wrong order. Christians should love all things that God has created, but the order in which these things are loved matters tremendously.

Ordo Amoris basically says it is okay to love things like comfort, but you shouldn't love it more than truth. Its okay to love money, but you shouldn't love money more than your fellow humans. When it is properly ordered, your love of money will be directed towards loving your fellow humans better instead of loving money for its own sake.

When the things you love are properly ordered, you actually love the lower goods more than if you placed the lower good at the top of the hierarchy. Take sexual pleasure for example. If you love sexual pleasure more then romantic love, you won't experience the necessary foundation that gives sexual pleasure meaning beyond the temporary moment. If you love romantic love more then sexual pleasure though, you build the foundation for a powerful relationship through which you gain security, trust, love, and meaning... Not just fleeting pleasure, which gives more power to both the physical pleasure and the life you build outside of it.

Another example is loving peace. We should love peace. But if you love peace more than you love your family, you won't be able to fight back if anyone tries to harm your family because you love peace more then them. And peace is created through its vigorous defense. Peace is not created by allowing evil to do whatever it wants.

At the very top of the hierarchy, what you should love more than anything else... Are God. Goodness itself. And the truth. Because this is what fundamentally gives you the ability to recognize good and evil. It gives you the ability to do the right thing no matter what.

Many of the evils of the world can be diagnosed by looking for what the individual, group, or society has chosen to love in a disorderly fashion. Woke people love the self and emotional comfort more than they love anything else, which blinds them to the truth and renders them incapable of loving others because they are too in love with themselves. By loving themselves more than anyone else, they make themselves incapable of being loved back, which deprives them of human connection and ultimately makes them miserable. But they can't see that, because they also love emotional comfort just as much as they love themselves. So they love the comfort of believing they are right about everything and cannot face the discomfort of admitting that they are wrong.
